title: Introduce compact credential-orbit and slim async-iterable stream UX
author: Anika Patel
release_notes: Adds a compact credential cascade (credential-orbit) with prioritized fallback and warmup hooks; introduces slim async-iterable stream helpers across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs (pause/resume, progress events, lightweight handshake presets); bumps SDK versions and updates docs. No breaking API changes for existing call sites.
description:
Context: Multiple customer engagements and internal integrations revealed friction when combining credential fallback, token warmup, and ergonomic stream consumption across our three SDKs. This PR introduces an opinionated but lightweight pattern called 'credential-orbit' (a compact cascade with warmup hook) and a matching set of 'slim async-iterable' helpers for streaming responses that unify behavior across Python, TypeScript, and Go.
Motivation: reduce boilerplate for users who need (1) safe credential fallback and warm connections, (2) pause/resume and progress callbacks for streaming consumers, and (3) consistent retry/backoff presets that play well with streaming handshakes.
Summary of changes: - Add credential-orbit: small orchestrator that accepts a prioritized list of credential providers, optional warmup callback, and a short-circuit fallback policy. Implemented in sdk core and exposed in each language SDK. - Introduce slim async-iterable stream helpers: Python AsyncIterator, TypeScript AsyncIterable factory, Go PullStream adapter. Features: graceful pause/resume, in-stream progress events (bytes/tokens), and a minimal handshake backoff preset tuned for short-lived connections. - Centralize three retry presets: aggressive (fast reconnect for transient infra), steady (default for user apps), conservative (longer cooldown for rate-limited contexts). Stream helpers wire these presets to the handshake/reconnect loop. - Add small ergonomic helpers: stream.withProgress(fn), stream.pauseable(), and stream.handshakeTimeout(ms) across the SDKs. - Docs and examples: quickstart snippets for the three SDKs and a migration note. - Version bumps: python -> 1.12.0, typescript -> 2.4.0, go -> 0.9.0.
Commits (high level): - feat(core): introduce credential-orbit orchestration and API surface - feat(py): async-iterator slim-stream + pause/resume + progress events - feat(ts): async-iterable factory, progress callbacks, handshake presets - feat(go): pullstream adapter, compact cred wiring - docs: examples and migration guide - test: cross-sdk integ tests for handshake/reconnect/resume - ci: add matrix job for stream presets and credential fallback
Changed files (illustrative): - sdk/core/cred/orbit.go - sdk/core/cred/orbit.py - sdk/core/cred/orbit.ts - sdk/python/redwood_stream/iterable.py - sdk/typescript/src/stream/slimIterable.ts - sdk/go/stream/pullstream_adapter.go - docs/sdk/streaming-quickstart.md - tests/integ/stream_handshake_matrix.yml - package.json (ts sdk bump) - pyproject.toml (py sdk bump) - go.mod (go sdk bump)
Review timeline and conversation: - 2026-02-18: PR opened by Anika Patel with initial cross-sdk patchset and integration tests. - 2026-02-19: Reviewer Mateo Ruiz: "Nice consolidation. One thing: the warmup hook runs synchronously today — that can add latency to the first request. Can we make warmup optional async and add a timeout?" Author reply (Anika): "Good point — added an async warmup signature and a default 150ms timeout; callers can override. Also added a test exercising a slow warmup provider." - 2026-02-20: Reviewer Jinsoo Park requested clearer semantics for pause/resume: "What guarantees do we provide if a consumer pauses mid-chunk?" Author reply: "We documented best-effort semantics and added a progress checkpoint so consumers can resume from the last complete token batch. Not guaranteed for every protocol, noted in docs." - 2026-02-22: Leah Carter: "Please add an opt-out that keeps legacy reconnect behavior for existing apps." Author: "Added config flag legacyHandshakeBehavior = true for each SDK; default is false so new ergonomics are opt-in on major bump. Documented migration steps." - 2026-02-24: All reviewers approved after follow-ups and minor test additions. CI: initial matrix run failed on Windows runner (flaky timeout in ts stream test). Reran the matrix; all checks green. CI summary: linux/py, linux/ts, linux/go, macos/ts, windows/ts matrix — all passed on final run.
Notes about compatibility: The public call signatures are additive; the credential-orbit API is an opt-in helper in each SDK. We bumped minor/patch versions and added migration notes; no breaking change flagged.
Performance: microbenchmarks show ~3% overhead for the warmup path (only when enabled) and ~6-8% lower latencies for resumed streaming flows due to reduced rehandshake in steady preset.
Merge: squashed and merged on 2026-02-25 by Mateo Ruiz (squash merge).
Related: ENG-2419 (UX for streaming), ENG-2427 (credential fallback improvements).
Follow-ups: - Backfill E2E tests for enterprise proxy scenarios (ENG-2473) - Consider exposing telemetry hooks for warmup timings (ENG-2491) - SDK release PRs: python & typescript & go release notes to ops.
